a9_6.name: head2_loss_weight
a9_6.not_promoted_reason: Raising global Head 2 loss pressure improved binary (more conservative routing, fewer FP) but REGRESSED attack-family and rare macro-F1; DoS F1 0.388->0.338, Shellcode precision 0.308->0.236, Analysis/Backdoor stayed near zero, attack FN rose.
a9_6.risk_observed: minority over-prediction lowered rare precision (precision-collapse pattern)
a9_6.lesson: Global attack_loss_weight is a blunt lever; more minority pressure does not separate overlapping families and hurts rare precision.

diagnosis.why_attack_family_weak: The 9-class macro-F1 is held near 0.50 by two near-zero classes (Analysis F1 0.0123, Backdoor F1 0.0704) plus a low-precision DoS (0.388). Analysis/Backdoor/DoS/Exploits form one mutually-confused cluster that overlaps in the 192-feature flow space by construction of UNSW-NB15: 70.8% of true Analysis and 70.2% of true Backdoor are absorbed into DoS, and Exploits<->DoS leak both ways (2076 + 1039). Because macro-F1 averages over the full fixed 9-class set, these collapsed classes each contribute ~0 and cap the mean. This is primarily an intrinsic feature-overlap + taxonomy property (RC1) compounded by severe imbalance (RC2), not a wiring, masking, or metric-inflation bug (independently verified clean in the A9.65 audit). The single linear Head 2 over a binary-dominated shared embedding (RC3) is the most actionable structural contributor, but A9.7/A9.8 showed capacity alone is within the noise band.
diagnosis.why_rare_class_weak: Shellcode (378) and Worms (44) have tiny absolute support. The sqrt-inverse-frequency class weights (Worms 3.95, Shellcode 1.33) buy high recall (0.77 / 0.66) at the cost of precision (0.31 / 0.22) because the rare label is over-assigned to confusable neighbours (Shellcode<->Recon/Fuzzers/Exploits). The bottleneck is precision, not recall; A9.6 confirmed that adding minority pressure lowers rare precision further. Rare macro-F1 also has very high seed variance (+/-0.0566 across A9 seeds).
likely_bottlenecks: RC1 (root cause): intrinsic Analysis/Backdoor/DoS/Exploits feature-space overlap; dominant macro-F1 limiter; largely not fixable by tuning.
RC2 (root cause): severe imbalance / tiny support for rare-hard families; low minority precision; high seed variance.
RC3 (most actionable structural): single linear Head 2 over a binary-dominated shared 128-d embedding; binary objective near-saturated while attack loss stays high.
RC4: official-partition prior shift (train/val benign 31.9% vs test 44.9%) inflates test binary FP and the val->test gap; intrinsic to the corrected protocol.
RC5: global attack_loss_weight is too blunt (explains A9.6); more minority pressure hurts precision without separating Analysis/Backdoor.
RC6: single-seed comparisons sit within a ~0.014 attack-family / ~0.057 rare noise band; require >=3 seeds.

Head 1 binary detector is already healthy (macro-F1 0.894, recall 0.949, only 5.1% attacks missed); it is NOT the primary bottleneck and end-to-end routed performance is capped mostly by Head 2 attribution, not Head 1 misses.
diagnosis.config_only_levers_status: Effectively exhausted. attack_loss_weight is config-wired but A9.6 proved a sweep fails. class_weight_max_clip is config-readable but NON-BINDING (max weight Worms 3.95 < cap 10). The val selection blend 0.5/0.5 is HARDCODED in hierarchical_evaluation.py (code change to alter). No focal loss, no attack-row sampler, and no per-class weight temperature/exponent hook exist (all require code). Therefore any meaningful next improvement requires a controlled code change.

recommended_next_experiment.id: A9.9 attack-family specialist router (prep first, then 1-seed screen, then 3-seed confirm)
recommended_next_experiment.idea: Keep the frozen A9 Head 1 binary detector as the router. Train a separate, dedicated attack-family specialist classifier on UNSW training ATTACK ROWS ONLY (richer non-linear Head-2-style branch), with train-only attack-row class handling. Detected attacks are routed into the specialist; report routed end-to-end and oracle attack-row metrics separately.
recommended_next_experiment.reason: It changes the task decomposition rather than re-pulling exhausted levers: it removes benign-vs-attack pressure from the family learner (addresses RC3), focuses capacity on the overlapping Analysis/Backdoor/DoS/Exploits boundaries, and protects the accepted binary detector (Head 1 frozen). The two cheap config levers (loss weight, capacity) already failed (A9.6/A9.7/A9.8); this is the highest-expected-value untried direction (A9.9 design rank 1) while staying honest about the ~0.60 intrinsic ceiling.
recommended_next_experiment.manual_run_count_note: 4 minimum = 1 one-seed screen + 3-seed confirmation (42/123/999); up to ~6 if a second specialist variant (train-only attack-row class-balancing or a precision temperature) is also screened before the 3-seed confirm.
recommended_next_experiment.screening_rationale: A one-seed screen de-risks the new specialist code path and gives a directional read cheaply; promotion requires a >=3-seed mean+/-std that clears the ~0.0143 attack-family noise band AND predefined success gates. Never promote on a single seed.
recommended_next_experiment.expected_benefit: Attack-family macro-F1 3-seed mean ~0.52-0.58 (stretch ~0.60); lift at least one of Analysis/Backdoor/DoS off the floor; protect rare macro-F1 (>=0.385669) and binary macro-F1 (~0.894, Head 1 unchanged).
recommended_next_experiment.expected_risk: Specialist overfitting on fewer attack rows; class-balancing can distort priors/calibration; routed end-to-end still capped by Head 1's 2,310 missed attacks; routed-vs-oracle metrics can be confused if documentation is careless; extra specialist artifact adds model-management complexity. Intrinsic RC1 overlap caps the achievable ceiling near ~0.60.
promotion_gates: attack_family_macro_f1 3-seed mean - A9 linear 3-seed mean > noise band (>= ~+0.015 and predefined margin)
no test-set tuning; validation-only selection/calibration; single final test

candidate_rankings.reason: Highest expected attack-family upside; decomposes the task, protects frozen Head 1; A9.9 design rank 1. Prep -> 1-seed screen -> 3-seed confirm.
Train shared model, freeze/partially freeze encoder, fine-tune Head 2 on attack rows. Backup to the specialist; harder to attribute and more overfit-prone.
Flatten/temperature the minority weights to lift rare PRECISION (opposite of A9.6). Cap alone is non-binding, so needs a code hook. Pairs well with the specialist.
Bias validation selection toward Head 2 (0.3 binary / 0.7 attack). Formula is hardcoded (code change). Selection-only; benefit bounded by the best attack-F1 epoch actually produced.
Focal loss on attack rows. Another minority/hard-pressure lever; A9.6 warns this risks rare-precision collapse. Only with strict precision-floor gates.
Calibrate Head 1 threshold on validation only to trade FP/FN. Does NOT help attack-family macro-F1; benefit bounded by the val->test prior shift (RC4). Threshold is hardcoded 0.5.

Train-only class-aware batching for minority exposure. Rare recall is already high; precision is the problem, so standalone benefit is weak/risky. Useful only INSIDE the specialist; project policy disables oversampling.
Prune/frequency-encode ultra-rare proto one-hots (133/192 features). Changes feature_dim, breaks direct A9 comparability, and carries leakage/reproducibility risk; full re-preprocessing required.
Optional grouped (Analysis/Backdoor/DoS/Exploits) reporting view to show separability ceiling. DIAGNOSTIC ONLY: must NOT replace the 9-class metric or relabel families to inflate numbers.
Already tested as A9.6 (1.5) and FAILED: attack-family and rare macro-F1 regressed. Do not repeat.
Already tested as A9.7 and confirmed across 3 seeds (A9.8): +0.0045 attack-family mean, within noise. Officially abandoned as the next major direction.

Legitimate stop option: given the intrinsic ~0.60 ceiling (RC1), accept A9 as the final UNSW model and advance to federated/security/XAI scope. Choose if the specialist screen does not clear the noise band.

one_seed_vs_multi_seed.reason: Attack-family macro-F1 carries ~0.0143 seed std and rare macro-F1 ~0.0566 (A9.8). A one-seed screen de-risks the new specialist code and gives a directional read; promotion decisions require a >=3-seed (42/123/999) mean+/-std that clears the noise band and the predefined gates. Never promote on a single seed.
